The **P.E.R.T. (Postsecondary Education Readiness Test)** is the College's placement test. It measures your reading comprehension, writing, and mathematics skills so you can be placed into the right developmental or college-level English, reading, and math courses.

Here's how to schedule it:

1. **Book an appointment** at the Assessment Center on the campus where you want to test, using the Calendly link for Massey (Fort Pierce), Pruitt (Port St. Lucie), Chastain (Stuart), or Mueller (Vero Beach).
2. **Walk-in option:** At the **Dixon Hendry Campus (Okeechobee)** you can start the P.E.R.T. MondayâThursday, 8:00 a.m.â5:30 p.m., without an appointment.
3. **Test at home:** You can take it remotely through **Honorlock** (24/7) if you meet the tech requirements â a desktop/laptop (no phones or tablets) with a working webcam, microphone, a stable connection, and current Google Chrome, plus your Indian River State College Student ID number.

A couple of useful details: your **first P.E.R.T. sitting is free** with the College, and each **additional sitting costs $20**. Bring a valid photo ID if you test in person.

Dual enrollment at Indian River State College lets a high school student earn college credit at the same time as high school credit, while still working toward a high school diploma. Here's how it works:

1. **Talk to your high school counselor** first to confirm you're eligible, get your GPA, and plan the credits you need for graduation.
2. **Apply to the College** and submit the Dual Enrollment Program Agreement (Form 508) with your application. Homeschool/PEP students submit additional agreements and enrollment verification instead.
3. **Submit placement scores** â take the P.E.R.T. at the College, or send official ACT/SAT scores (no more than two years old), or use alternative placement measures. You'll be required to complete a mandatory orientation.
4. **Register for approved courses** through The River Portal. Classes are on the College's approved Dual Enrollment course list, and you'll work with an assigned academic advisor to build your plan before your second semester.
5. **Pick up textbooks** â public and charter students get them free through their district (return them each semester); private school, homeschool, and PEP students use their College bookstore account by the published deadline.

A few things worth knowing:
- **Where and when:** Courses are offered at the College's five campuses, at many local high schools, online/hybrid, before/during/after the school day, or in summer. You can't register for a class that overlaps your high school schedule.
- **Transfer:** Dual enrollment college credit transfers to any public college or university offering that same course with the same prefix and number â but if you don't stay at the College, another school can't be guaranteed to accept it.
- **Key dates (Spring 2027):** The last day to submit a Spring 2027 application is **December 1, 2026**, and the last day to register for Spring 2027 classes is **December 15, 2026**.

For details, see the [Dual Enrollment program page](https://irsc.edu/programs/special-programs/dual-enrollment/) and the [Dual Enrollment courses list](https://irsc.edu/admissions/admissions-process/dual-enrollment-courses). For questions you can reach the Dual Enrollment team at **DE@irsc.edu**, or use [The River Line](https://irsc.edu/advising-services/riverline/) for advising help. There isn't an income threshold for Florida residency at Indian River State College. Residency for tuition purposes is based on where you've lived, not how much you earn â to qualify for in-state tuition you (or your parent/guardian, if dependent) must show legal Florida residency for at least 12 consecutive months before the first day of classes, be a U.S. citizen or eligible non-citizen, complete the Florida Residency Declaration, and submit the required residency documents (see the Florida Residency Requirements page).

You may be thinking of financial aid instead â programs like the Promise Program or certain grants can have income/FAFSA criteria, but that's separate from residency. If you tell me which program (in-state tuition, Promise, a grant, or federal aid), I can look up the exact eligibility rules for that one.

The Indian River State College application fee depends on your program:

- **$20** â Most programs, including A.A., A.S., career training, technical certificates, and adult education (ESL & GED)
- **$30** â Bachelor's degree programs and selective admission programs
- **$60** â A.S. Nursing

The fee is non-refundable, and some programs may add extra fees. Details are on the [Apply to Indian River State College](https://irsc.edu/admissions/apply/) page and in the [admissions FAQ](https://irsc.edu/faq/).

Because dates shift each term, check the [Fall 2026](https://irsc.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current/catalog/academic-calendar/fall-2026) or [Spring 2027](https://irsc.smartcatalogiq.com/en/current/catalog/academic-calendar/spring-2027) calendar for your term, and confirm your specific deadline in The River Portal before you drop.
